newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower as soybeans falter.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower as soybeans falter.

text.p: CBOT soy products ended lower on Thursday, in line with a slide in soybean futures, on lackluster USDA export data and on rains in Brazil soybean growing regions, traders said.

"There was more rain and the exports weren't very good," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter, referring to overnight rains in Brazil. "All that's weighing on beans, and beans are pulling everything else down."
Rains fell overnight in portions of Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul soybean growing region, dousing fears of drought-related crop losses.

USDA's export sales report showed the soyoil net export sales tally at 19,500 tonnes, above trade expectations for 4,000 to 7,000 tonnes. The soymeal total at 62,400 tonnes was near the low end of expectations for 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes.

Commercial buying in soyoil limited losses. Cargill Inc bought 900 lots March soyoil, 400 lots July and 100 May. Produce Grain and Term Commodities each bought 400 March. Rosenthal Collins sold 1,000 lots March soyoil.
Soyoil closed down 0.24 to 0.20 cent per lb with March off 0.24 at 23.87 cents. Soymeal ended down $3.60 to $1.80 per ton with March down $2.90 at $237.50.

In soymeal trade, Cargill Inc sold 400 lots March and Farmers Commodities Corp and Term Commodities each sold 200 March, traders said. Prudential Securities bought 800 March and sold 400 March while SAK Futures bought 400 March.
